purpose: Premise check performed BEFORE building any London-open breakout strategy: does MGC (gold futures, COMEX) show a volume/volatility cluster around the London session open, comparable to the NY-open cluster already implicitly assumed by H004 (ORB_v1)? User explicitly questioned whether session-open breakout logic even applies to futures given ~23h/day trading.
data_source: First-ever outside_rth=true fetch this project (all prior intraday fetches used outside_rth=false, RTH-only). MGCV6 (contract_id 744880158, COMEX), step=FIFTEEN_MINS, step_count=1000 (max).

window.note: ~17 calendar days -- SHORTER than the ~46-day/1000-bar depth for RTH-only 15min bars (data/metadata/depth_assessment.json), because 24h/day bars consume the same 1000-bar cap in fewer calendar days.

method: Grouped all bars by UTC hour-of-day; computed average bar volume and average (high-low) range per hour across the full window, then repeated independently on a chronological split-half (first ~8.5 days vs second ~8.5 days) as a robustness check against a single sub-period dominating the result.

sanity_checks.maintenance_break: hour 21 UTC (5-6pm ET) shows 0 bars in both halves -- correctly reflects CME/COMEX daily maintenance break, confirms data integrity
sanity_checks.holiday_check: 2026-09-07 (Labor Day, US holiday) shows reduced daily volume (21251 vs ~35000-49000 typical) but does not change the qualitative hourly pattern -- NY-open hours still dominate in the half containing this date

conclusion: PREMISE REJECTED for MGC. London open (~07:00-08:00 UTC during BST) is one of the LOWEST-volume windows of the 23h session (238-409 contracts/bar), not elevated at all. NY cash equity open (~12:00-14:00 UTC) is unambiguously the dominant volume/volatility cluster (890-1423 contracts/bar, 2.7x-4.6x London-open levels), consistent in both independent halves of the sample. Building a London-open ORB variant on MGC would be testing a strategy whose own economic premise already fails a direct empirical check. Not proceeding to build H014 as a full strategy on this instrument.
caveats: Sample is short (~17 days, 44 observations per hour) and single-instrument (MGC only, chosen for its plausible London/gold-fix linkage) -- this is a premise check, not a definitive claim that no futures product ever shows a London-open effect.
naive_t_stat / formal significance testing not applicable -- this is a descriptive volume/range comparison, not a strategy backtest with trades.

MES and MCL were not checked -- MES (US equity index) has no plausible London-session linkage and MCL (WTI crude) is priced more by US/Cushing dynamics than London hours, so neither was considered a priori as likely as MGC for this specific mechanism.
